perspective:
Bradley’s accessible/subjective information includes:

- He knows he is Bradley Ochoa, a salesperson at a marketing firm, and that Katherine Lasiloo is the marketing manager and his colleague. He has experienced their professional relationship as generally cordial but sometimes strained by disagreements over traditional sales versus digital marketing.
- In their meeting, he has prepared data and charts from the last five campaigns to support traditional sales methods. He tells Katherine he appreciates her digital strategies but believes core sales would benefit more from traditional methods.
- He hears Katherine say she sees his point but that the market is evolving and digital outreach cannot be ignored. She asks how he reconciles his data with increasing online engagement.
- He replies that he is not suggesting abandoning digital marketing; he is frustrated that proven traditional methods feel sidelined without proper consideration.
- He hears Katherine say she understands his frustration, that it is about balance, and that they should analyze the data together to integrate both approaches.
- After the meeting, Katherine shares recent digital campaign success stories. Bradley hears that these campaigns significantly boosted engagement and sales.
- He asks Katherine to explain how those digital strategies are developed.
- He hears Katherine explain that it is about targeting the right audience with the right message, and she walks him through the analytics and decision-making behind a recent campaign.
- He admits he had doubts about moving away from traditional methods, but seeing the outcomes makes him want to understand the digital approach.
- He hears Katherine say she is glad he is open to exploring it, that it is important to adapt and evolve with market trends, and that they should dive deeper into the data.
- Bradley proposes a joint strategy meeting to integrate traditional and digital marketing strategies.
- He hears Katherine agree, saying combining strengths could lead to better results and suggesting they schedule time to brainstorm and outline next steps.
- He says he is hopeful that leveraging both their expertise can create something impactful, and he appreciates her willingness to collaborate.
- He hears Katherine say she looks forward to it and that it is about leveraging each other’s strengths.
- After the joint meeting, Bradley is excited and works overtime to prepare a board presentation integrating both ideas.
- He tells Katherine he has integrated both their ideas into a draft and is excited about the potential.
- He hears Katherine say the draft looks comprehensive and well thought out, and that his hard work shows.
- He says he is convinced the integrated approach will set them apart from competitors and that he wants to nail the presentation.
- He hears Katherine say she is confident they will succeed with that level of preparation and suggests going through it once more to fine-tune.
- After the presentation and implementation, Bradley feels grateful for his professional growth and the successful collaboration with Katherine.
- He tells Katherine he cannot thank her enough, has learned much, and is grateful for the growth he experienced through their collaboration.
- He hears Katherine say it has been a pleasure seeing their project come to fruition and that his openness to new ideas made it a successful partnership.
- Bradley proposes regular strategy sessions to continue their collaboration.
- He hears Katherine agree, saying regular sessions will keep them on top of their game and market trends, and that they should do it.
